evals.prompt: Draft a short blog post intro (2-3 paragraphs) about why small teams ship faster, and save it to blog/why-small-teams-ship-faster.md.
evals.expected_output: A 2-3 paragraph intro written in the fallback house style: no gratuitous dash connective, no AI-tell vocabulary, no bot scaffolding, contractions and varied sentence rhythm, concrete over vague, and no invented evidence.
expectations: The file blog/why-small-teams-ship-faster.md exists with a 2-3 paragraph intro on the requested topic.
The prose contains no em-dashes or en-dashes (the — and – characters appear nowhere in the new file).
None of the AI-tell words appear: delve, leverage, utilize, tapestry, realm, landscape, testament, robust, seamless, synergy, paradigm, crucial, pivotal.
No bot scaffolding: no 'In conclusion', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'Firstly', 'Let's dive in', 'Without further ado', 'Buckle up'.
The prose uses contractions naturally (at least one of don't/it's/you'll/that's or similar) and mixes short sentences with longer ones rather than a uniform rhythm.
The post does not invent studies, metrics, named customers, or causal certainty that the prompt did not provide.

evals.prompt: draft/launch-post.md reads like AI wrote it. Make it sound natural and human — edit the file in place. Keep everything factually true.
evals.expected_output: The draft is rewritten in place in the requested natural style: gratuitous dashes, AI-tell vocabulary, bot scaffolding, performed-casual phrasing, manufactured punch and closure, the orchestra analogy, and decorative bold are gone; the hedge pile is cut; but the one load-bearing caveat (Postgres 14+ only, older versions silently return incomplete results) survives, and the post still announces the same product with the same claims.

files.name: draft/launch-post.md
files.description: AI-sloppy launch post: em-dashes, 'delve'/'leverage'/'tapestry'/'robust'/'seamless'/'utilizes'/'crucial'/'paradigm shift'/'testament', performed-casual phrasing, a cadence-only contrast and verbless parallel, significance tails, unsupported value verbs, summary buttons, 'In today's fast-paced world', 'Furthermore', 'In conclusion', 'Buckle up', 'Let's dive in', an orchestra analogy, decorative-bold bullet leads, a hedge pile ('results may vary and every data stack is different and your mileage may depend') wrapped around ONE load-bearing caveat: Postgres 14+ only, older versions silently return incomplete results.

expectations: draft/launch-post.md was edited in place and contains no em-dashes or en-dashes.

The AI-tell words are gone from the revised file: delve, leverage, tapestry, robust, seamless, utilizes, crucial, paradigm, testament, unlock, empower, transform (or replaced with concrete plain wording supported by the source).

The bot scaffolding is gone: 'In today's fast-paced world', 'Furthermore', 'In conclusion', 'Buckle up', 'Let's dive in' appear nowhere; the orchestra analogy is removed rather than reworded into another analogy.

The performed or cadence-only phrases are gone: 'Here's the thing', 'isn't just another analytics tool', 'completely different way to work', 'Same warehouse, radically better decisions', 'which is exactly what makes it work', 'The result?', and 'In short: data finally feels human' appear nowhere. Their unsupported interpretations are deleted rather than rephrased into new slogans, while the concrete product claims remain.

The load-bearing caveat SURVIVES in substance: the revised post still says QueryPilot requires Postgres 14 or newer and that older versions silently return incomplete results (any phrasing); the surrounding throat-clearing hedges ('results may vary', 'every data stack is different', 'mileage may depend') are cut.
The post still announces the same product and claims (no invented features, no dropped sections beyond trimming); the revision reads as edited prose, not a from-scratch different post.

evals.prompt: Clean up site/customers.md so it doesn't read AI-generated — but the customer quote must stay exactly as written, word for word.
evals.expected_output: The surrounding prose is de-AI'd, but the block-quoted customer testimonial (which itself contains an em-dash and the word 'leverage') is byte-identical to the original — quotes are preserved verbatim even when they contain AI tells.

files.name: site/customers.md
files.description: Customers page whose surrounding prose is saturated with AI tells, containing one block-quoted customer testimonial from 'Dana R., VP Engineering at Coastline Freight' that itself includes an em-dash and the word 'leverage' — a trap: the verbatim-preservation rule outranks the em-dash and vocabulary rules inside quotes.

expectations: The block-quoted customer testimonial (the '> "We rolled it out in a week...' lines including the Dana R. attribution) is byte-identical to the fixture: its em-dash and the word 'leverage' inside the quote are untouched.
The prose OUTSIDE the quote no longer contains: leverage, synergies, delve, robust, seamless, crucial, paradigm, tapestry, 'Furthermore', 'In conclusion', 'it's worth noting', or em-dashes.
The page still makes sense as a customers/testimonials page (heading and quote retained, surrounding copy rewritten rather than deleted wholesale).

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for the current change and commit it.
evals.expected_output: Negative control: a normal, precise commit message for the retry-attempts change (e.g. mentioning the 3 -> 5 default change) and a commit — with no prose-pass ceremony, no rules recitation, and no rewriting beyond the commit message itself.

files.name: src/retry.js
files.description: Committed retry helper with an uncommitted working-tree change: default attempts bumped from 3 to 5.

expectations: The change is committed with a message that accurately describes the actual diff (the retry attempts default changing from 3 to 5).
No prose-editing pass is performed or announced: the session does not apply or mention the natural-writing rules, and src/retry.js's content is committed as-is (no rewording of code or comments).
No new prose files or revision reports are created.

evals.prompt: Reword the headline in site/index.md to be shorter — just that one line.
evals.expected_output: Negative control for scope: the H1 headline is shortened; every other line of the file is byte-identical; no full-document prose pass, no revision report file.

files.name: site/index.md
files.description: Landing page with a long H1 headline, two body paragraphs, and a pricing line. Only the headline should change.

expectations: The H1 headline line is rewritten to something shorter that keeps the meaning (automatic weekly changelogs).
Every line of site/index.md other than the headline is byte-identical to the fixture (git diff shows changes only on the heading line).
No revision-report HTML file is generated and no full-document rule-by-rule pass is announced.

evals.prompt: Edit draft/security-note.md in place so it sounds natural, preserving the literal attack sample exactly. Also create revision-report.html so I can inspect what changed.
evals.expected_output: The article is de-AI'd without changing the literal attack sample, and the requested revision-report.html is generated through the bundled safe report builder. The report embeds its data as base64 rather than placing the hostile </script><script> sequence into executable markup.

files.name: draft/security-note.md
files.description: Tell-heavy security blog draft containing a literal </script><script> attack sample that must remain exact in the Markdown but be safely encoded inside the report.

expectations: draft/security-note.md is edited in place; AI-tell vocabulary/scaffolding is removed while the literal `</script><script>window.pwned=true</script>` sample remains byte-identical in the Markdown.
revision-report.html is created and contains Original, Revised, and Diff report data for this edit.
The bundled scripts/build_revision_report.py helper is used (visible in tool calls), rather than manually inserting raw prose into a JavaScript object.
The exact hostile sequence `</script><script>window.pwned=true</script>` does not appear raw in revision-report.html and the __DATA_BASE64__ placeholder is gone; the data is embedded as base64.
No temporary report-data JSON file is left behind unless explicitly requested.

evals.prompt: Revise drafts/sync-engine-post.md for our engineering blog. The content is right but readers keep saying it's confusing to follow. Fix what makes it hard to read.
evals.expected_output: The revision fixes the grounding failure, not just style: the draft leans on two unintroduced concepts early ('the reconciler' is used in paragraph 1 but only explained in the final paragraph; 'drift windows' is used twice and never explained anywhere). The revised post either moves the reconciler explanation before first use or adds a one-line grounding at first mention, and introduces 'drift windows' at or before its first use. Meaning, epistemic force, and voice are preserved; the fallback style adds no gratuitous dashes or AI-tell vocabulary. No revision report is generated because the user did not ask for one.

files.name: drafts/sync-engine-post.md
files.description: A ~5-paragraph technical blog draft. Paragraph 1 says user edits 'go straight to the reconciler before hitting storage' with no explanation of what the reconciler is; the explanation ('the reconciler is the background process that merges concurrent edits into one ordered log') appears only in the final paragraph. 'Drift windows' is used in paragraphs 2 and 4 and never defined. Otherwise clean prose with no AI tells, so the ONLY real fix needed is grounding/order.

expectations: The revised draft introduces or explains 'the reconciler' before (or at) its first use: either the explanation moved earlier or a one-line grounding was added at first mention; the reader no longer meets the term cold.
'Drift windows' is defined at or before its first use in the revised draft (a short in-place grounding is sufficient).
The grounding was done in place: no appended glossary section or terms table was bolted onto the post.
The author's meaning and technical claims are preserved (the reconciler explanation content survives; no invented behavior).
No new AI tells were introduced: no em/en-dashes and none of the tell words (delve, leverage, utilize, tapestry, robust, seamless, crucial, pivotal) appear in the revised draft.
No revision-report HTML or report-data JSON was created because the user did not explicitly request a report.
